scope: native x86 assigned-AP reset and Linux re-online as CPU-reclamation proof
review_limit: explicitly supported native x86 AP profile; source/design only

accepted_design.reset_primitive: export the existing Linux send_init_sequence(apicid) as an attempted reset only; do not add SIPI
accepted_design.reclamation_proof: successful synchronous device_online from the retained known-offline CPU identity, followed by identity and cpu_online revalidation
accepted_design.locking: retain CPU policy and device-hotplug exclusion; hold CPU read exclusion for validation/reset effects, release it and restore preemption before sleepable device_online
accepted_design.failure_rule: any failed or uncertain reset/online retains every owner and a per-CPU progress ledger; never compensate to guest-running after INIT

required_order: close admission and retain exact generation, CPU/device identities, module pins, guest allocations and IRQ-work storage
quiesce all guest and host producers
validate completed original Linux offline state and retained device/APIC identity
issue per-AP INIT assert/deassert with preemption disabled
perform sleepable Linux device_online without CPU read exclusion
require device_online success and revalidate identity plus cpu_online for every assigned CPU
drain and unpublish callbacks, IRQ-work, workers and mappings before storage release or generation reuse
blocking_followups: implement the reset/re-online journal as a separate shutdown primitive rather than reusing ordinary hotplug rollback
implement exact per-generation Linux IRQ-work publication inventory, unpublish and callback drain
test wrong, BSP and online targets; partial reset; online failure/no-op; identity change; repeat recovery; concurrent hotplug; pending IRQ publication without IPI; callback drain and generation reuse
establish the explicitly supported APIC, firmware and hypervisor profile
